title: Space Tech Briefing — September 11, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts! It is Friday, September 11, 2026, and you are locked in for your daily dose of the latest and greatest from the final frontier! Let's power up our morning with a quick look back at some truly remarkable recent developments in space technology and exploration.

First up, let's celebrate a monumental achievement in our search for other worlds. NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, better known as TESS, has just unveiled its most complete view of the starry sky to date! This incredible exoplanet hunter, launched in 2018, has been diligently scanning the cosmos for planets orbiting distant stars. The recently published vast mosaic is a testament to its dedication, constructed from observations made between April 2018 and September 2025. It skillfully combines 96 sectors of the sky, revealing nearly 6,000 colorful objects that represent confirmed or candidate exoplanets. What an incredible step forward in mapping our cosmic neighborhood!

And speaking of incredible journeys, we're thrilled to recap some exciting news for human spaceflight! French astronaut Thomas Pesquet has officially begun his intensive training for his next mission, slated for 2027. Get ready to cheer him on, because Thomas is set to take command of the Vast-PAM-1 mission, heading directly to the International Space Station! It's always inspiring to see our astronauts preparing for their next great adventure among the stars.

That's all for your morning briefing today, September 11, 2026! Thank you for joining us, and keep looking up!
